tools.name: html_render
tools.description: Show Ben a table, cards, a chart, a timeline, a diagram or a side by side inline in this thread, above your reply, instead of typing it out. It is cheap: a simple table or a row of cards is enough, and it does not have to be a full page. Pass a self-contained HTML document (inline <style> and <script>, no local files): <!doctype html>, a few lines of <style> and the markup will do. It runs sandboxed, sized to its content, and can be interactive. Do not announce the page or repeat its rows in your reply. A report or document to keep goes into the artifacts folder as a file instead. Use the theme variables on :root, never fixed colours, so the page matches Omni in light and dark: --background, --foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --border, --primary, --primary-foreground, --accent, --accent-foreground, --destructive, --warning, --success, --code-background, --chart-1, --chart-2, --chart-3, --chart-4, --chart-5, --chart-6, --radius, --font-sans, --font-mono. The frame is the reply column (about 680px on desktop, 360px on a phone) on the thread background. Leave html and body with no background, outer card, border, page title banner or side padding: the base sheet sets text colour and font. A box that needs its own background gets var(--card), 16px padding and var(--radius) corners. Give charts a fixed pixel height and fluid width. Use --chart-1 to --chart-6 in that order for series, and label them or add a legend: never colour alone. Let the content set the height: no vh units and no height:100% on html or body.

title.description: A short name for the page, like "Commits by package".
